proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed an informal total finite-sample honest continuum band and matching all-band converse on the declared horizon, including Lipschitz and thinning extensions; five standard probability lemmas were verified against source text. D0.5 stopped below the field floor at incremental tier because the exponent-range extension and explicit calibration introduce no new rate transition or inference mechanism; independent validity review confirmed that the below-cutoff design-moment program is new research rather than an in-scope repair. Formalization was never entered, so there is no Lean proof certificate; predecessor-source underspecification and comparator/prior-art positioning findings remain unresolved.
tldr: Natural-course subtraction cancels the response level in the causal gain curve of an exact deterministic dose floor. For the public positive-radius response ball with \(\beta\in[1,2]\), measurable power-envelope designs with \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and every horizon \(n^{-1/\{2(\kappa+1)\}}\le\Delta_n\le\bar\delta\), the finite-sample minimax expected maximum full width of a \(90\%\)-honest connected continuum band is \(W_n\asymp r\). A single total band with computable public tuning attains this order; an all-band converse matches it. The rate has a boundary-slope regime, with a derivative-free Lipschitz endpoint, and an effective-entropy regime. The common-domain rate is inherited from the gain-band predecessor; the delivered extensions are the endpoint and previously excluded thinning regimes, together with explicit finite-sample calibration.
gap: The banked gain-band theorem occupies matched-order inference for \(\beta\in[3/2,2]\), \(2\beta>\kappa+1\). It leaves the endpoint class and executable numerical calibration outside its delivered contract. Published regression and honest-inference results supply the methods but do not supply this finite-sample exact-floor gain-band decision rule.
fill: The target is a matched all-band frontier over the enlarged parameter family, with a public conditional-coefficient calibration and a deterministic envelope on every failed-design branch. Inherited cancellation and localized entropy are supporting inputs, with their prior ownership explicit.
